title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Deployment Guide, Reference Architecture, Packaging, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade & Rollback, and Customer Requirements
author: Ava Chen
content:
Summary:

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended practices, reference architectures, packaging requirements, day-2 operational procedures, upgrade & rollback playbooks, and a customer requirements checklist for Private Deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for platform engineers, field solutions engineers, and customer site reliability engineers responsible for installing and operating Redwood Private in regulated or network-isolated environments.

Scope:
- VPC (cloud-hosted private deployment with customer networking)
- On-prem / air-gapped installations (colocated or customer datacenter)
- Day-0 install, Day-2 operations, upgrades, and rollback procedures
- Packaging and artifacts delivered to customers
- Customer requirements library (networking, access, compliance artifacts)

Audience and prerequisites:
- Audience: Platform, Infra, and Customer SRE teams.
- Required skills: Kubernetes administration (k8s 1.23+ LTS recommended), Helm, basic networking, TLS/KMS/HSM concepts, NFS/S3-like object storage.
- Test environment: isolated dev cluster that mirrors customer network policies.

Minimum system requirements (reference):
| Component | Minimum | Recommended | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Kubernetes | 1.23 | 1.26 LTS | Control plane HA strongly recommended |
| CPU | 8 vCPUs | 32 vCPUs | Control-plane + small runtime; worker sizes depend on model footprints |
| GPU (for inference nodes) | 1 x A10 / A100 equivalent | 4 x A100 / H100 | Model size / throughput dependent |
| Memory | 32 GB | 256 GB | Per GPU node: 256GB for large models |
| Disk | 200 GB SSD | 2 TB NVMe | Local scratch for KV cache and swap; persistent storage for logs/backups |
| Object storage | S3 or compatible | S3 with lifecycle | For model artifacts and backups |
| Network | 1 Gbps | 10 Gbps | Low latency between inference nodes is important |

Reference architectures (high level):
1) VPC (cloud private deployment)
- Components: Customer VPC, private control plane (customer-managed or Redwood-managed control plane endpoints), data plane (k8s cluster), internal load balancers, NAT gateways, VPC peering or Transit Gateway for multi-VPC connectivity, KMS integration for secrets.
- Recommended layout: Three-tier subnets (public bastion/NAT, private control, private data plane) across at least 2 AZs for HA.
- Network considerations:
  - Allocate /22 CIDR to avoid IP pressure (adjust by scale).
  - Internal ALB/NLB for API and model endpoints (internal only).
  - Security groups: separate SGs for bastion, control plane, inference nodes, metrics/observability.
  - Egress: explicit egress via NAT or VPC endpoints for S3 and container registries.

2) On-prem / Air-gapped (customer datacenter)
- Components: Customer network, firewall rules to allow approved registries, airgap bundle served over internal registry, optional bastion with jumpbox, on-prem object store (MinIO) or S3 proxy, HSM/KMS on network, external load balancer or metal LB (e.g., Metallb).
- Deployment model: Kubernetes (Rancher / OpenShift / vanilla k8s) with storage class for models and persistent volumes.
- Connectivity: If no external egress, provide an airgap tarball plus internal registry and package repository.

Component mapping (service names):
- control-plane: redwood-controller (Helm chart: redwood/control-plane)
- data-plane: redwood-runtime (inference pods, autoscaler)
- observability: redwood-prometheus, redwood-loki, redwood-grafana
- ingress: internal-nlb / metallb + envoy-ingress
- model-store: s3/minio + model-index service
- secrets: Kubernetes secrets backed by KMS/HSM integration

On-prem packaging & delivery checklist:
- Deliverables (customer-facing package):
  1. Airgap bundle (.tar.gz) containing images, Helm charts, CRDs, operator binaries.
  2. Helm chart release (values.yaml template).
  3. Installation guide and preflight checklist (this doc).
  4. Systemd/service wrapper or Kubernetes manifests for non-k8s installs (rare).
  5. Verification scripts and smoke tests (kubectl/helm based).
  6. Support bundle collection script (redwood-support-collector.sh).

- Packaging constraints:
  - Images must be signed (cosign) and checksums provided.
  - Include provenance metadata.json with component versions and SHA256 checksums.
  - For restricted customers, deliver FIPS-compatible builds where requested.

Example Helm values snippet (values.yaml fragment):
```yaml
replicaCount: 3
image:
  repository: internal.registry.example.com/redwood/runtime
  tag: v2026.11.0
service:
  type: ClusterIP
  port: 8080
resources:
  requests:
    cpu: "2000m"
    memory: "8Gi"
  limits:
    cpu: "8000m"
    memory: "32Gi"
modelStore:
  s3Endpoint: https://minio.internal.svc.cluster.local
  bucket: redwood-models
kms:
  provider: aws-kms # or hsm
  keyId: alias/redwood-deploy-key
```

Preflight checklist (Day-0):
1. Verify cluster k8s version and node capacity.
2. Confirm network CIDR, route tables, and firewall ports (see ports table below).
3. Confirm registry access (or have airgap bundle).
4. Provision KMS/HSM access and service principal with least privilege.
5. Create S3 bucket and test object PUT/GET.
6. Ensure TLS certificate for internal API endpoints (or generate self-signed for PoC).
7. Confirm observability endpoints (Prometheus scrape access, Loki ingest endpoints).

Ports and firewall requirements (minimal):
| Source | Destination | Port | Protocol | Purpose |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Bastion / Admin | Control plane API | 6443 | TCP | k8s API |
| Control plane | Worker nodes | 10250 | TCP | kubelet |
| Clients | Ingress | 8080 / 443 | TCP | API / TLS |
| Nodes | Object store | 9000 | TCP | MinIO / S3 API |
| Prometheus | Metrics endpoints | 9090/9100 | TCP | Metrics |

Installation procedure (VPC):
1. Create VPC and subnets as per reference architecture.
2. Provision a k8s cluster (EKS/GKE/AKS) with given node groups (GPU node pool).
3. Provision IAM roles and KMS keys and grant minimal privileges for the redwood service account.
4. Configure internal registry access (ECR/Artifact Registry) or push airgap images.
5. Apply network policies and security groups (least privilege).
6. Install observability stack (Prometheus, Loki, Grafana) and verify scraping.
7. Install Redwood control-plane via Helm: helm repo add redwood https://charts.redwood.ai && helm upgrade --install redwood-control redwood/control-plane -f values.yaml
8. Verify control-plane pods reach Ready and can talk to runtime components.
9. Perform smoke test: curl --unix-socket /var/run/redwood.sock "http://localhost:8080/health" or kubectl port-forward svc/redwood-api 8080:8080 && curl http://localhost:8080/health

Installation procedure (On-prem / Airgap):
1. Validate preflight checklist and collect manifests from customer environment (kubeadm / kubeconfig).
2. Load images to customer registry: for image in images.txt; do skopeo copy docker://$image docker://internal.registry/$image; done (or use provided load-images.sh).
3. Apply Helm charts using local registry references.
4. Create KMS / HSM integration per customer instructions (mount PKCS#11 provider or configure KMS plugin).
5. Install model-store (MinIO) and import model artifacts.
6. Run verification smoke tests and collect initial logs bundle.

Day-2 operations (ongoing):
- Monitoring & Alerts (recommended thresholds):
  - Model inference latency p95 > 500ms -> Severity P2 Alert
  - Request error rate > 1% over 5m -> P1 Alert
  - Node GPU memory utilization > 90% -> P2 Alert (scale/evict)
  - Control-plane API error rate 5xx > 0.5% over 5m -> P1
  - Prometheus ingestion lag > 1m -> P3

- Regular maintenance tasks:
  1. Weekly: verify backups of model-store and config (test restore monthly).
  2. Monthly: rotate KMS keys as per customer policy and update secrets.
  3. Quarterly: capacity review (node sizing, pod density, autoscaler tuning).
  4. After any incident: run regression tests including prompt set evaluations.

- Scaling and autoscaling guidance:
  - Use HPA for control-plane horizontal scaling where applicable.
  - Use custom autoscaler for GPU nodes based on queue depth and pending pods.
  - Batching: tune runtime batch_size and max_wait_ms per workload to balance latency and throughput.

Upgrade & rollback playbook:
- Principles:
  - Always perform upgrades in staging that mirrors customer production.
  - Use canary/blue-green deployments for control-plane + runtime when possible.
  - Keep at least one prior release artifacts available for rollback.

- Upgrade steps (control-plane):
  1. Create a snapshot: kubectl get all --all-namespaces -o yaml > pre-upgrade-<ts>-snapshot.yaml
  2. Tag a canary workload (1% traffic) to new release via helm set or service routing.
  3. Monitor canary for 30-60 minutes (latency, error rate, resource usage).
  4. If safe, gradually expand rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) using traffic routing or helm batch upgrades.
  5. Post-upgrade validation: run end-to-end smoke tests, run model quality checks against canonical prompt set.

- Rollback triggers:
  - Canary p95 latency regression > 2x baseline or absolute > 1s for interactive workloads.
  - Error rate > 1% sustained for 5-10 minutes.
  - Resource exhaustion (OOM, GPU OOM, crashloop) on > 1% of pods.

- Rollback commands (Helm):
  - Check history: helm history redwood-control -n redwood
  - Rollback: helm rollback redwood-control <REV> -n redwood
  - For CRD or DB changes that are not reversible, follow the emergency rollback checklist (contact Redwood field SRE).

Emergency rollback checklist:
1. Pause ingress traffic to the new release (set ingress to previous candidate or divert to fallback region).
2. Execute helm rollback to prior stable release.
3. Revert any schema migrations if reversible; if not, restore from backup (coordinate with Redwood support).
4. Run smoke tests; re-open traffic only after greenchecks.
5. Capture verbose logs and create a postmortem entry.

Customer requirements library (short matrix):
| Requirement | Customer-provided Artifact | Implementation note |
|---|---|---|
| Network CIDR and peering | Network diagram + ACLs | Required for VPC and on-prem connectivity setup |
| TLS certificates | Valid SAN cert covering internal hostnames | Redwood can provide CSR guidance |
| KMS/HSM access | Key policy + service principal | Provide least-privilege roles |
| Container registry | Registry endpoint + credentials or airgap delivery | If airgapped, provide images list |
| Object storage | S3 endpoint and credentials | Lifecycle and backup policy specified |
| Compliance docs | SOC2 / ISO contacts | For restricted customers, mark data flows and retention |

Ownership and contact points:
- Installation owner: Private Deployments team (eng-private-deployments).
- Primary contact for escalations: eng-private-deployments-oncall@redwood.ai (monitor 24x7 for P1s).
- Field SRE: Diego Martinez (primary), Priya Patel (backup).

Post-install validation suite (smoke tests):
1. Health-check API success (200).
2. Simple text generation inference (short prompt).
3. Model load/unload sequence (ensure KV cache warmed and released).
4. Observability: Confirm Prometheus scrape, Loki log ingestion, Grafana dashboard metrics populate.

Appendix A - Example smoke test commands:
```bash
# Port forward the API and run health check
kubectl port-forward svc/redwood-api -n redwood 8080:8080 &
curl -sS http://localhost:8080/health | jq
# Run a simple inference test
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rw-1.0-small","prompt":"Hello world"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
```

Appendix B - Troubleshooting quick hits:
- Pods stuck Pending: check node taints and GPU labels; run kubectl describe pod to see scheduling reasons.
- High tail latency: check batch_size and max_wait_ms, reduce batch size for latency-sensitive routes.
- Secret access errors: verify KMS role and secret-controller logs.
